Map residues across species through Ensembl Compara's gene-tree alignments

proteins_map_residues.Rd

Map a residue of one protein to the residue of another protein in the same column of Ensembl Compara's gene-tree alignment, or say why there is none, for a batch of queries.

Answers which mouse residue is human p53's Ser15? Ensembl Compara has already aligned every protein of each gene tree, across all its species, to build the tree. A residue's column in that alignment is the published answer. This wraps mzLib's ComparaGeneTreeAlignment (mzLib #1465): Load reads Compara's peptide alignment of every gene tree, keeping the canonical proteins of your species' genes, and MapResidue answers each query: which residue of the target protein sits in the same alignment column as residue position of the source protein. Local files only; nothing is downloaded.

Usage

proteins_map_residues(queries, alignment, gene_trees, gtfs = NULL, gene_sets = NULL,
  proteins = FALSE, timeout = NULL)

Arguments

queries

The (source protein, position, target protein) queries, one result row each, in this order, duplicates included: a data.frame with three columns, source_protein_id, position and target_protein_id, or a list of list(source_protein_id, position, target_protein_id). The ids are Ensembl protein stable ids; the position is a whole number, the 1-based residue in the source protein. They travel on stdin after the species lines.

alignment

Compara's peptide alignments, Compara.<release>.protein_<collection>.aa.fasta.gz (908 MB for protein_default in release 116), from emf/ensembl-compara/homologies/. Required.

gene_trees

Compara's gene-tree file of the same release, <collection>.GeneTree_content.default.e<release>.txt.gz. It names each gene's tree and its canonical protein. Required.

gtfs

A named character vector from species to its Ensembl primary-assembly GTF, as for proteins_build_orthology: c(homo_sapiens = "Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.116.gtf.gz"). Only the genes in these are kept, and so only their canonical proteins. NULL (the default) with no gene_sets: mzLib's default keeps every gene in the gene-tree file - millions for the vertebrates - and a caveat says so. The answers for your species' proteins are the same.

gene_sets

Instead of a GTF, a compact gene table mzLib's EnsemblGeneSetWriter made from one, by species in the same way. A species may be in gtfs or gene_sets, not both.

proteins

Also return the kept proteins with their ungapped sequences, as proteins. FALSE (the default): proteins is NULL.

timeout

Seconds to allow, or NULL (the default) to wait: for human, mouse and rat at release 116 the whole call takes about a minute, nearly all of it reading the alignment.

Details

Every query gets exactly one outcome, mzLib's own name for it: "Aligned" (with the column, the target position and its residue), "GapInTarget" (no target residue in that column - never the nearest one), "DifferentAlignments" (the proteins are in different gene trees), or "SourceNotInAlignment" / "TargetNotInAlignment" (that protein was not kept: only each gene's canonical protein is aligned).

Positions are Ensembl's. To start from a UniProt position, align the UniProt sequence to the canonical Ensembl protein with proteins_align first, and align the target's Ensembl protein to its UniProt sequence after. proteins = TRUE returns the Ensembl sequences for that.

A position outside the source protein fails the whole call. mzLib's MapResidue throws for it rather than returning an outcome, and mzLibR passes positions through unchecked, so keep them within each source protein: with proteins = TRUE, a sequence's length is its last valid position.

Value

An mzlibr_residue_mappings.

records is a data.frame with one row per query, in the order given: source_protein_id, position (the 1-based residue in the source, as given) and target_protein_id, as given; outcome, one of the five outcomes above; column, the source residue's 1-based column in the gene tree's alignment, NA when the two proteins share no alignment; target_position, the 1-based position of the target's residue in that column, in the target's ungapped sequence, NA unless "Aligned"; and target_residue, the target's residue there, one letter, NA unless "Aligned". It may be a different amino acid from the source's: a column pairs homologous positions, not identical ones.

row_count counts the queries, one row each (queries). outcome_counts is a named vector, outcome to the queries with it (queries), every outcome present in mzLib's order, zeros included. column_names lists the table's columns.

alignment is a list describing the alignment file: source_file_name; sha256, of the file's bytes as read (the compressed bytes for a .gz); release and collection, read from the file name (NA when the name carries none); alignment_count, the alignments in the file, one per gene tree, kept proteins or not (alignments); protein_count, the canonical proteins kept (proteins); and restricted_to_gene_tree_content, the sha256 of the gene-tree file whose canonical proteins were kept, the same as gene_trees$sha256.

gene_trees is a list, as proteins_build_orthology reports it: source_file_name, sha256, release, collection, member_count, the genes kept from the file (genes), and restricted_to_gene_sets, the gene sets' sha256s, or NULL when no gene set was given and every gene was kept.

gene_sets is a data.frame, one row per species given (none without gtfs or gene_sets): species, source_file_name, sha256, release, genome_build and genebuild_last_updated (NA when the GTF's name or headers carry none), and gene_count, in genes, every biotype.

proteins_included says whether proteins = TRUE was given. proteins is NULL without it; with it, a list: row_count (proteins kept), column_names, and records, a data.frame with one row per kept protein in order of protein id: protein_id, the Ensembl protein stable id; alignment_index, which alignment holds it (1-based in R, in file order; two proteins share a column only when they share this); tree_id, its gene's Compara gene tree; and sequence, its residues with the alignment's gaps removed, the sequence every position counts in. setNames(m$proteins$records$sequence, m$proteins$records$protein_id) gives the sequences by id, for proteins_align. caveats names this call's traps: gene trees read unrestricted, files named for different releases or for none, queries naming a protein the alignment did not keep.

What each outcome means

"Aligned": the target has a residue in the source residue's column; column, target_position and target_residue are set. "GapInTarget": the target has a gap in that column, so no residue corresponds; column is set, the target's are NA. "DifferentAlignments": the two proteins are in different gene trees, so this alignment says nothing about them. It does not say they are unrelated. "SourceNotInAlignment" and "TargetNotInAlignment": that protein was not kept - not in the file, not its gene's canonical protein, or outside your gene sets. Another isoform is never mapped through the canonical one.

The traps

A position past the end of the source protein fails the whole call with mzLib's message (for example "ENSP00000269305 has 393 residues."), as an mzlib_usage_error, and no row is returned, not even for the queries that were fine. A source protein that was not kept is an outcome, "SourceNotInAlignment", checked before the position. Use Ensembl ids and Ensembl positions: a UniProt accession is "SourceNotInAlignment", never an error. Use the alignment and the gene trees of one release: mzLib does not compare them, and a gene's canonical protein and tree can change between releases. Keep Ensembl's file names, so the result can report the release each one carries. Sharing a gene tree is not orthology: a tree holds paralogs too, so ask proteins_build_orthology which genes are orthologs, then map their residues here. **Check target_residue** before carrying a modification across: a phosphosite on S is not a site on A.

Wraps

Parameters: units, ranges and defaults

alignment

path; required. Compara's peptide alignments of its gene trees, emf/ensembl-compara/homologies/Compara.RELEASE.protein_COLLECTION.aa.fasta.gz (plain or .gz): one gapped multiple alignment per tree, as FASTA, separated by a // line. Read with ComparaGeneTreeAlignment.Load, which keeps only the canonical proteins of the genes kept from gene-trees, and checks every row's characters and width whether it is kept or not. 908 MB compressed for protein_default in release 116.

gene_trees (wire --gene-trees)

path; required. Compara's gene-tree membership dump, COLLECTION.GeneTree_content.default.eRELEASE.txt.gz (plain or .gz), read with ComparaGeneTreeContent.Load. It names each gene's tree and its canonical protein (the row flagged Y), which is the only protein of the gene the alignment holds.

wire --species

string[]; default absent; range >= 0 lines; each exactly three tab-separated fields. Read from stdin (not an option), first: one line per species, the species' Ensembl production name (homo_sapiens), a tab, gtf or gene-set, a tab, and the path, exactly as genes orthology reads them. gtf is an Ensembl primary-assembly GTF, read with EnsemblGeneSet.LoadGtf; gene-set is the compact table mzLib's EnsemblGeneSetWriter makes from one, read with EnsemblGeneSetReader.Load. Their only use is ComparaGeneTreeContent.Load's restrictTo: only the genes in them are kept, and so only their canonical proteins. None (the stdin starts with –): mzLib's default, restrictTo null, keeps every gene in the gene-tree file and every canonical protein in the alignment, millions for the vertebrate collection, and a caveat says so. A species listed twice, a kind other than gtf or gene-set, or a missing file is a usage error. Not an argument here: rendered from gtfs and gene_sets, two named character vectors from Ensembl production name to path, one stdin line per species (none: mzLib keeps every gene).

queries

string[]; required; range >= 1 line; each exactly three tab-separated fields. Read from stdin (not an option), after a line holding only –: one query per line, the source protein's Ensembl stable id, a tab, a 1-based residue position in it, a tab, and the target protein's id (ENSP00000269305, 15, ENSMUSP00000104298). One row per query, in input order, duplicates included. The position is parsed as an integer and passed to MapResidue unchecked; the bridge does not compare it with the protein's length.

proteins

flag; default FALSE. Also return the kept proteins (ComparaGeneTreeAlignment.Proteins: id, alignment, tree and ungapped sequence), so a protein's Ensembl sequence can be aligned to a UniProt sequence with proteins align without a second file. Absent: proteins is null.

Returned fields

Each field with its type, its unit, and what NA means when it is NA.

alignment

object; never NA. The alignment file and what was kept from it (typed under result.tables.alignment).

gene_trees

object; never NA. The gene-tree file and what was kept from it, the same fields as genes orthology's gene_trees (typed under result.tables.gene_trees).

gene_sets

map<string,object>; never NA. Species to its gene set, in ordinal order of species, each with genes resolve's gene_set fields (typed under result.tables.gene_sets). Empty when no species lines were given.

row_count

int; in queries; never NA. Rows: the queries, one each.

outcome_counts

map<string,int>; in queries; never NA. Outcome to queries with it, every ComparaColumnOutcome in mzLib's declaration order, zeros included.

column_names

string[]; never NA. The mapping table's columns in order.

records (wire columns)

table; never NA. Column name to one value per query, in input order.

proteins_included

bool; never NA. Whether --proteins was given.

proteins

object; NA when --proteins was not given. {row_count, column_names, columns}: one row per kept protein, in ordinal order of protein id (typed under result.tables.proteins).

caveats

string[]; never NA. This call's traps: gene trees read unrestricted (every gene kept), an alignment and gene-tree file named for different releases or for none, queries naming a protein the alignment did not keep.

Columns of records

source_protein_id

string; never NA. The query's source protein id, as given.

position

int; never NA. The query's 1-based residue position in the source protein, as given.

target_protein_id

string; never NA. The query's target protein id, as given.

outcome

string; never NA. mzLib's ComparaColumnOutcome name, verbatim: Aligned (the target has a residue in the source residue's column), GapInTarget (the target has a gap there: no residue corresponds, never the nearest one), DifferentAlignments (the two proteins are in different gene trees, so the alignment says nothing about them), SourceNotInAlignment or TargetNotInAlignment (that protein was not kept: not in the file, not a canonical protein, or outside the gene sets). Exactly one per query.

column

int; NA when the two proteins do not share an alignment (DifferentAlignments, SourceNotInAlignment or TargetNotInAlignment). The source residue's 1-based column in the gene tree's alignment. Set for Aligned and GapInTarget.

target_position

int; NA when the outcome is not Aligned. The 1-based position of the target's residue in that column, in the target's ungapped sequence.

target_residue

string; NA when the outcome is not Aligned. The target's residue there, one letter as the alignment writes it. It may differ from the source's residue: a column pairs homologous positions, not identical ones.

Fields of alignment

a list.

alignment$source_file_name (wire source_file_name)

string; never NA. The file's name (ComparaGeneTreeAlignment.SourceFileName).

alignment$sha256 (wire sha256)

string; never NA. Lower-case hex sha256 of the file's bytes as read, the compressed bytes for a .gz (SourceSha256).

alignment$release (wire release)

string; NA when the file name does not start Compara.RELEASE.. The Ensembl release parsed from the file name (Release).

alignment$collection (wire collection)

string; NA when the file name does not match Compara.RELEASE.COLLECTION.aa.fasta. The collection parsed from the file name, e.g. protein_default (Collection).

alignment$alignment_count (wire alignment_count)

int; in alignments; never NA. Alignments (gene trees) in the file, kept proteins or not (AlignmentCount).

alignment$protein_count (wire protein_count)

int; in proteins; never NA. Proteins kept (Count): the canonical proteins of the genes kept from gene-trees that the file holds.

alignment$restricted_to_gene_tree_content (wire restricted_to_gene_tree_content)

string; never NA. The sha256 of the gene-tree file whose canonical proteins were kept (RestrictedToGeneTreeContent); the same as gene_trees.sha256.

Fields of gene_trees

a list, as proteins_build_orthology() reports it.

gene_trees$source_file_name (wire source_file_name)

string; never NA. The file's name.

gene_trees$sha256 (wire sha256)

string; never NA. Lower-case hex sha256 of the file's bytes as read (compressed for a .gz).

gene_trees$release (wire release)

string; NA when the file name carries no .eRELEASE.txt suffix. The release parsed from the file name.

gene_trees$collection (wire collection)

string; NA when the file name does not start COLLECTION.GeneTree_content.. The Compara collection, e.g. vertebrates.

gene_trees$member_count (wire member_count)

int; in genes; never NA. Genes kept from the file (ComparaGeneTreeContent.Count): those in the gene sets, or every gene when none was given.

gene_trees$restricted_to_gene_sets (wire restricted_to_gene_sets)

string[]; NA when no species lines were given: every gene in the file was kept. The sha256s of the gene sets the members were restricted to, in ordinal order (RestrictedToGeneSets).

Fields of gene_sets

a data.frame, one row per species, species first.

source_file_name

string; never NA. The GTF's file name; for a gene-set table, still the GTF's.

sha256

string; never NA. Lower-case hex sha256 of the GTF's bytes as read; the value genes resolve and genes orthology report for the same GTF.

release

string; NA when the GTF's file name carries no release. The annotation release from the GTF's name.

genome_build

string; NA when the GTF has no #!genome-build header. e.g. GRCh38.p14.

genebuild_last_updated

string; NA when the GTF has no #!genebuild-last-updated header. The header's value.

gene_count

int; in genes; never NA. Genes in the set, every biotype.

Fields of proteins$records

a data.frame, one row per kept protein, inside the proteins list.

protein_id

string; never NA. The Ensembl protein stable id, as the alignment's header gives it (ComparaAlignedProtein.ProteinId).

alignment_index

int; never NA. Which alignment holds it, 0-based in file order (AlignmentIndex). Two proteins share a column only when they share this.

tree_id

string; never NA. Its gene's Compara gene tree, e.g. ENSGT00950000183153, from gene-trees (TreeId).

sequence

string; never NA. The protein's residues with the alignment's gaps removed (Sequence): the sequence positions count in.

Errors

Each is an R condition carrying the class shown and mzlib_error; see mzlib_error.

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

--alignment or --gene-trees missing or given without a value; a value after --proteins

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

no line holding only – on stdin, or no queries after it; a species line that is not species, tab, gtf or gene-set, tab, path; a species listed twice; a query that is not three tab-separated fields, or whose position is not an integer

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

a GTF, gene-set table, gene-trees file or alignment that does not exist (checked before any input is read)

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

mzLib's MapResidue refused a query's position as outside the source protein (ArgumentOutOfRangeException): 0, negative, or past its last residue. The message names the query and quotes mzLib, which gives the protein's length. The whole call fails on the first such query, in input order, and no row is returned. A source protein that is not kept is an outcome, SourceNotInAlignment, checked before the position.

mzlib_bridge_error (correctness)

a file mzLib's reader refuses (InvalidDataException, naming file and line): in the alignment, a sequence line before any header, an empty header, a character that is not a letter, * or -, rows of different widths, an empty alignment, a kept protein twice, or an alignment whose kept proteins belong to two gene trees; in the gene-tree file, a row without four cells, a flag other than Y or N, or a kept gene in two trees or without exactly one canonical protein; a GTF gene row without gene_id

mzlib_service_unavailable (service_unavailable)

Never raised by this verb.

Caveats

  • A column pairs positions that Compara's alignment puts together, which is homology, not identity: the target residue may be a different amino acid, so check target_residue before carrying a modification across (a phosphosite on S is not a site on A).

  • Only each gene's canonical protein is in the alignment (the gene-tree row flagged Y). A query naming another isoform's Ensembl id is SourceNotInAlignment or TargetNotInAlignment, never mapped through the canonical one. To start from a UniProt position, align the UniProt sequence to the canonical Ensembl protein with proteins align first, then map, then align the target's canonical protein to its UniProt sequence: three steps, each of which can meet a gap.

  • A gap is GapInTarget, never the nearest residue: no residue of the target sits in that column.

  • DifferentAlignments means the two proteins are in different gene trees, so this alignment says nothing about them. It does not say the genes are not homologous, nor that they are orthologs when they share one: a tree holds paralogs as well, so read orthology from genes orthology.

  • mzLib's MapResidue throws for a position outside the source protein instead of returning an outcome, so one such query fails the whole call, and the bridge does not check lengths for it. Keep positions inside each source protein; --proteins gives each kept protein's sequence.

  • mzLib does not compare the alignment's release with the gene-tree file's. Use the two files of one release: a gene's canonical protein and its tree can change between releases. The envelope reports the release each file name carries, and a caveat says when they differ or one is absent.

  • Every input is read whole, and the alignment keeps only the canonical proteins of the genes kept, so give the species' gene sets: with none, every gene in the gene-tree file is kept (millions for the vertebrate collection), and so every canonical protein of the alignment.

Performance

ComparaGeneTreeAlignment.Load reads the whole alignment file once, checking every row, and is the cost; mapping a query afterwards is a binary search. For human, mouse and rat at release 116 (64,114 proteins kept from 54,308 alignments), mzLib #1465 reports about 33 s to load, and this bridge measured 55 s for the whole call on 2026-10-28, reading the three GTFs, the gene-tree file and the alignment. Give all of a batch's queries to one call. Neither load takes a degree of parallelism, so there is no --threads. Every call starts one bridge process, which costs a .NET start-up before any work.

Same verb in other bindings

  • Python (pyMzLib): pymzlib.proteins.map_residues

  • Rust (mzLibRust): mzlib::proteins::map_residues_with with MapResiduesOptions

  • R (mzLibR): proteins_map_residues

Since

Wire protocol 1; pyMzLib 0.7.0; mzLibRust 0.1.0; mzLibR 0.1.0.

Not yet verified

The spec records these as open. They are listed rather than hidden:

  • The outcome is mzLib's ComparaColumnOutcome name verbatim (Aligned, GapInTarget, ...), as classify-peptides projects PeptideSharing. genes orthology's statuses are snake_case because mzLib names them (OrthologySnapshot.StatusName). PUSH-TO-MAINLAND: a ComparaGeneTreeAlignment.OutcomeName helper in the same style; when it lands the wire names change to its spelling, a breaking change to call out.

  • MapResidue throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException for a position outside the source, which fails a whole batch. PUSH-TO-MAINLAND: a non-throwing outcome (PositionOutsideSource) so one bad query is one row. Until then the bridge projects the throw and does not check lengths itself.

  • mzLib compares no release between the alignment and the gene-tree content (OrthologySnapshot.Build does, for the dumps). PUSH-TO-MAINLAND: ComparaGeneTreeAlignment.Load could refuse a gene-tree content named for another release, as Build refuses one; the bridge only reports it as a caveat.

  • result.tables (alignment, gene_trees, gene_sets, proteins) is not validated by tools/check_verbs.py, which checks only envelope_fields, columns and bulk. Bridge tests pin each nested object's keys (GenesMapResiduesTests).

  • Not yet ported to mzLibRust or mzLibR; the binding names above are proposals.

References

  • doi:10.1101/gr.073585.107: Ensembl Compara gene trees, each built on a multiple alignment of its member proteins, the alignment this verb reads columns from (Vilella et al. 2009, Genome Res 19:327)

  • doi:10.1093/nar/gkaf1239: Ensembl releases, their GTFs and the Compara gene-tree files (Ensembl 2026, NAR)

See also

proteins_align for the UniProt legs, proteins_build_orthology

Examples


# A real cut of Ensembl release 116: the TP53 and GAPDH gene trees' alignments, with the human,
# mouse and rat rows exactly as Ensembl publishes them.
gtfs <- c(homo_sapiens = "Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.116.gtf",
          mus_musculus = "Mus_musculus.GRCm39.116.gtf",
          rattus_norvegicus = "Rattus_norvegicus.GRCr8.116.gtf")
site <- proteins_map_residues(list(list("ENSP00000269305", 15, "ENSMUSP00000104298")),
  alignment = "Compara.116.protein_default.aa.fasta.gz",
  gene_trees = "vertebrates.GeneTree_content.default.e116.txt.gz", gtfs = gtfs)
site
#> <mzlibr_residue_mappings> 1 queries through Compara.116.protein_default.aa.fasta.gz (Ensembl 116, 5 proteins kept)
#>   Aligned 1
# Human p53's Ser15 is mouse p53's Ser18:
site$records[, c("outcome", "column", "target_position", "target_residue")]
#>   outcome column target_position target_residue
#> 1 Aligned    476              18              S
c(site$alignment$release, site$gene_trees$collection)
#> [1] "116"         "vertebrates"
